film.title: The Poor Man's Cheesecake: Steubenville, Cold Cheese and the Valley That Won't Fold
film.description:
In 1945 Primo DiCarlo came home from the war and opened a pizza shop on South Third Street in Steubenville, Ohio. The pies came out of sheet pans in squares, and the cheese went on cold, after the oven. Nobody, not even the family, knows exactly why. Back then people called it the poor man's cheesecake.

We asked the three schools we cover within an hour of Steubenville. Robert Morris sends us to Police Station Pizza in Ambridge. Duquesne holds court at Beto's in Beechview. And Youngstown State says Brier Hill pizza was here first, with no cold cheese and barely any cheese at all. Who's crazier? That's the whole Ohio Valley: contrarian, defensive, proud, and long left out of the national story.

A Hardwood Bricks Productions film, in association with JuiceboxNationTV Entertainment. A 19 North Films film. Written and narrated by Matthew Hagan; some narration uses his HeyGen AI avatar. Lauren McAllister, Barnaby St. Clair and Brett Callahan are fictional AI anchors and are not affiliated with Robert Morris, Duquesne or Youngstown State. Comments are paraphrased from public posts with names withheld. Key & Peele, "Loco Gangsters" (Comedy Central), excerpt used for commentary. Original music.

Sources: The Takeout (Danny Palumbo, 2023); PMQ Pizza Magazine (2018); Herald-Star, "History in the Hills" (Paul Zuros, 2020); WVPB / Inside Appalachia (Zack Harold, 2022); Pittsburgh City Paper; Food Republic (2025); Business Journal (2015); Wikipedia, "Ohio Valley-style pizza" and "Brier Hill-style pizza".

reels.title: Who's crazier: Steubenville or Youngstown?
reels.text: Steubenville puts the cheese on cold. Youngstown's Brier Hill pizza barely uses cheese at all. Our Youngstown State desk says do the math.

reels.title: Why does Steubenville pizza get cold cheese?
reels.text: Ohio Valley pizza: baked in a sheet pan, sold by the square, cheese on after the oven. Even the DiCarlo family doesn't know why.
